unit.title: Preparing for the Oral History Interview

contentBlocks.text: You have a real question list. Today: the listening skill that turns a list of questions into a genuine conversation.

ਧਿਆਨ ਨਾਲ ਸੁਣਨਾ (listening with attention) means genuinely following what's said, not just waiting for your turn to ask the next question. The best oral-history moments often come from a natural follow-up question, asked in response to something the person just said, not from your original list. For example, if your elder mentions a specific place while answering a ਬਚਪਨ question, a natural follow-up might be 'ਉਹ ਥਾਂ ਕਿਹੋ ਜਿਹੀ ਸੀ?' (What was that place like?) — a question you couldn't have planned in advance. Take one question from your Day 2 list and write one likely follow-up question you might ask, depending on how your elder answers.

This skill — genuinely listening and following up — is what separates a real conversation from reading off a list. Tomorrow we'll cover the practical and respectful side of actually recording an interview.

objectives: Explain ਧਿਆਨ ਨਾਲ ਸੁਣਨਾ (active listening) and why it matters in an interview
Write a genuine, unplanned follow-up question responding to a hypothetical answer
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review Day 2's question list.
2. Introduce active listening and the natural-follow-up-question idea.
3. Model one example follow-up together.
4. Have the child write their own follow-up question from a Day 2 question.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview tomorrow's topic: recording and consent.
differentiationTips: Struggling: role-play a short exchange together (teacher answers a Day 2 question, child practices asking a real-time follow-up out loud) before writing it down
Ready for more: ask them to explain why a planned follow-up question is different in kind from a genuinely spontaneous one
Every Gurmukhi word used in this lesson was checked against gurmukhifix's Lexicon before writing
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. ਧਿਆਨ ਨਾਲ ਸੁਣਨਾ means genuinely following what's said, not just waiting to ask the next question. 2. The best follow-up questions respond to something specific just said, which couldn't have been planned in advance.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's 'oral-history capstone' description, building the conversational listening skill a real interview genuinely depends on, beyond just a prepared question list.
